source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade / Downgrade HIB-CPLD firmware by Redfish when system is off
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade FPGA firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully after BMC reset only one time.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl (Redfish REST client, on the BMC side) + HIB-CPLD image (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- HIB-CPLD downgrade via Redfish (system is off): the agent needs the exact user-provided HIB-CPLD image first the host must be powered OFF first (flash while system is off), then runs the Redfish update flow: `PATCH /redfish/v1/UpdateService` (set preserve/replace behavior), `POST /redfish/v1/UpdateService` to upload the image, poll the returned TaskService task to completion, then `GET /redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory` to confirm the new version is active. Not a single one-liner; run step-by-step after the image is placed on the BMC.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the full Redfish PATCH/POST response, the TaskService poll loop, and the final `FirmwareInventory` JSON so the user confirms the HIB-CPLD version changed and the SUT powers on cleanly after the off-state flash.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: HIB-CPLD firmware flash via Redfish is state-changing and can brick the BMC/host if interrupted; flash only the user-specified image with host powered off for a clean result, and never interrupt mid-flash.

original_test_intent: The row appears intended to update HIB-CPLD through Redfish with the host off, but the Procedure explicitly instructs an FPGA firmware operation, so the hardware destination is not authoritative.
original_method: PATCH Immediate apply, POST an unspecified file to a generic assumed UpdateService URI, wait, permit an undefined single BMC reset and read generic FirmwareInventory without a component selector.
manual_activity: Platform/RD must correct the target component and define its activation/recovery owner before an authorized engineer can approve any destructive API plan.
required_inputs: Master-source decision selecting HIB-CPLD or FPGA
Secure authentication, stable power and target-specific recovery
safety_requirements: Do not upload any image while Items/Script and Procedure identify different programmable devices.
Do not use generic UpdateService without an advertised component selector or validated image manifest target.
Reject embedded root credentials and TLS bypass; never retry/reset after an uncertain write.
Recovery must match the corrected device and remain accessible if that device or BMC management fails.
agent_execution_scope: After correction, discover the component-specific action, validate immutable device/image binding and execute one approved transition with correlated task/reset and independent activation evidence.
Do not PATCH, POST, reset or assign a verdict while target semantics conflict.
engineer_actions: Correct HIB-CPLD versus FPGA scope and align Items, Procedure, Script and evidence.
Approve device/image/state/security/recovery plan and issue final verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its HIB-CPLD assumption follows Items/Script but silently overrides the source Procedure. Generic task/inventory wording does not prove device selection.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No write is authorized. After source correction, use a secure vendor-advertised action that explicitly binds the image to the corrected device and correlates task/activation status.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The HIB-CPLD Items/Script versus FPGA Procedure, host-off state, source PATCH/POST/GET, one-reset criterion and 10/30-minute values remain verbatim.

modernized_recommendation.status: PENDING HIB OR FPGA TARGET CORRECTION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correct the device identity, bind a signed image to its exact board/inventory member, discover a component-specific vendor action, execute one approved transition/reset plan and verify active target plus host/BMC health independently.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the corrected HIB-CPLD or FPGA target on a confirmed platform.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record corrected device/board/image, BMC/Redfish schema and recovery-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor update, activation and recovery documentation for the corrected programmable device.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds authoritative target and component selection while removing unsafe authentication and assumed endpoint behavior.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Prevents programming or validating the wrong device and adds target-specific recovery/health evidence.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Owner source correction and vendor device contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: HIB-CPLD and FPGA are not interchangeable; no project override may silently choose one.

project_override_considerations: Projects may supply versions, images and vendor action only after Master Source names the target. An override cannot reinterpret the Procedure without an explicit source decision.
expected_evidence: Approved source correction naming one programmable device
Advertised component selector/action and redacted correlated task transcript
Post-update target inventory and affected link/platform health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Script identify HIB-CPLD while the Procedure explicitly says FPGA firmware. Because the POST has no component selector and Criteria use generic FirmwareInventory, neither field can safely resolve the destructive target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Hardware destination is essential operation semantics, not a missing project parameter. Executing either interpretation could program the wrong device, so the case is blocked pending source correction.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Its HIB-CPLD interpretation remains historical only and is not accepted as a silent source fix.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED is retained with the explicit component-identity conflict as the primary reason.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates the true destructive-target block from ordinary missing images, credentials and power parameters.

review_improvement: Requires component-bound routing and target-specific activation evidence before any Redfish write.
independent_technical_reasoning: The software mechanism could be fully automated after correction, but automation cannot choose between HIB-CPLD and FPGA. With a generic image variable and inventory query, an HTTP success could represent the wrong programmable device.
